<!-- pr-reviewer: efd1f264d0c1924ffed4a5da1b75afee81170e4e -->
## Independent review of PR #204 (facing-flat axis candidates)

**Verdict: BLOCKING (1 item).** The pole candidates are fine. The least-trimmed-squares re-centring in `try_pole` turns a part that `main` refuses into a **trusted wrong axis**.

### BLOCKING 1: the LTS step locks onto a finely meshed minority, and `judge` doesn't catch it

Scenario (probe, built in a throwaway worktree, not committed): a plate 100 x 100 x 10 (`box`, two triangles per face, the usual STL export) with a turned boss r5 h10 at (20, 20) on top (72 segments x 5 bands).

| | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | refused: "the model's normals share no rotation axis" |
| PR head | `Ok`, dir (0.667, 0.667, 0.333), origin (1.11, 1.11, -4.44), `trusted = true`, `outlier_share = 0.013` |

The real turned feature is the boss, about Z at (20, 20). The PR's axis is nowhere near it, and the one revolved feature on the part is the 1.3 % it set aside.

What happens (I instrumented `try_pole`):
1. The pole Z (top and bottom faces) fails plain `try_axis`. The boss drags the LS line to about 1.4 mm, just past the tolerance. That drag was the evidence the part is not a revolve about the plate.
2. LTS takes the median **by facet count**, not by area: `sorted[sorted.len() / 2]` over facets. The boss has 792 of the 804 facets but 1.3 % of the area, so it decides "the half that misses least". The settled line was origin (0.28, 0.28) with 444 of 804 facets kept.
3. `judge` then passes on every facet. The box's side faces are two triangles each, so their circumcenters sit at the face centres and every side normal line meets ANY line through the box centre. That is about 99 % of the area, and the tolerance is 3 % of rho (about 48), so about 1.45 mm. The boss's 72 bearings pass the coarseness gate for any direction.
4. `refine_dir` and `try_axis` then tilt it to the box-centre-to-boss diagonal, which passes the same way.

So the claim in the doc comment, "the re-centred line must still pass the full judgement on every facet, so this can only find an axis the part earns", does not hold. `judge` is a necessary test, not a sufficient one. A prismatic body whose face lines meet at a point passes it around any direction once a small, finely meshed round feature supplies bearings. On `main` the plain-LS drag was what kept such parts out, and LTS removes it.

Possible fixes, author's choice:
- weight the trimmed median by area, not count;
- require the kept half to carry a real share of the answering area (for example `MIN_KEPT_SHARE`, as `reweigh` does);
- keep LTS only for the case it was built for: `iso`, or a pole whose plain line fails by a small margin.

Pin it with this plate-plus-off-centre-boss fixture (refused by name).

### Other scenarios probed (PR head vs main)
- Hex bar on end, h 10/20/40/200, 1 and 5 bands: refused on both. With h 40 and up, the three side-pair flats outrank the caps for `MAX_POLES = 3`, so the caps are never tried. This only causes false refusals, so it is safe.
- L-bracket: refused on both.
- Plate with a centred turned hole (r20/r40 t10, r45 t30): Z at the hole on both. r45 t30 was refused on main and is fixed by the PR. Correct.
- Upright plate (big flat normal Y) with a Z boss of several sizes, 1 and 5 bands: Z on both. The Y pole is tried and rejected. Correct.
- D-flat bars (r10, various h, flat depths, 1 and 5 bands): refused on both. The flat's radial normal never wins, so there is no wrong axis.
- Discs and short bars, r50 h10/h20 (L/D 0.1-0.2) and r10 h5..h60, single-band too: Z on the PR. Single-band r10 h10/20/30 and a tilted (1,1,1) off-origin r10 h30 were refused on main and are now correct. This is a good gain.
- Ball with two perpendicular flats: now reads Z with 5-7.5 % set aside (main: refused). Arguable but consistent with how D-flats are treated, so not blocking.

### Pre-existing on main, not caused by this PR (worth an issue)
- Plate + boss r5 h10 at (10, 0): **main** already returns a trusted 45-degree axis (0.707, 0, 0.707). Same mechanism: box-face point concurrency, then `refine_dir`.
- A long single-band shaft (r10 h150) with a D-flat (normal X) and a cross hole along X reads **X** on main and on the PR (`trusted`, aside 0.042). The single-band wall lines meet at one point, and the cross hole supplies the bearings about X.

Both mean `judge` can't tell point concurrency (box faces, single-band walls) from line concurrency.

### Checks
- Eigen candidates win exact ties: yes. They come first, and the comparison is a strict `<`.
- Determinism: the cells sum in data order, and the sort uses `total_cmp` with the cell key as tie-break. Fine.
- No-panic and NaN: normals are filtered finite before they reach the cells, and the `i64` casts are guarded by `is_finite`. `sorted.len() < 2` guards the median index, `unit` handles a zero sum, and every fallible step uses `?`. Fine.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib axis` on the PR head: 42 passed.

Not approved, not merged.

Blocker fixed in 7fff05c (pushed; `origin/main` merged in first as 2c4a7fe).

The least-trimmed-squares re-centring in `try_pole` now has three guards. I kept all three; none of them broke a pin.
1. The trimmed half is taken by the **area**-weighted median, not the facet count.
2. The kept half must hold `MIN_KEPT_SHARE` (0.5) of the answering area on at least `MIN_KEPT` (8) facets. These are the same constants as in `axis_robust::reweigh`, now `pub(super)`.
3. The re-centring runs **only when the normal moment is isotropic**. Elsewhere a pole candidate whose plain line fails is declined, just as on main.

Guard 3 is the one that refuses your plate: its moment is not isotropic. Guards 1 and 2 protect an isotropic part the same way.

Pin: `axis_poles::tests::a_plate_with_an_off_centre_boss_is_refused_by_name`. It builds a 100 x 100 x 10 plate (two triangles per face) with an r5 h10 boss at (20, 20), 72 segments x 5 bands, and expects "share no rotation axis". On the previous head efd1f26 it fails with your exact axis, (0.667, 0.667, 0.333) through (-1.11, -1.11, 4.44).

The earlier pins all still pass: the punched r10 x 40 bar, the L/D 2 and L/D 1.5 bars, the cube and the sphere.

Gate:
- motion: the lib tests plus `multiaxis`, `multiaxis_avoid`, `multiaxis_rough`, `rotary`, `rotary_adaptive`, `rotary_links` and `rotary_offset`.
- app: `drilling_cross*`, `lathe_*` and `turning*`.

That is 29 binaries, all green. Clippy on motion and app (all targets) has 0 warnings.

I left alone the wrong axes you found that are already on main (a boss at (10, 0) read as 45 degrees, and a single-band shaft with a D-flat read as X). The coordinator is filing those separately.

## Re-review of PR #204 at 7fff05c

**Verdict: BLOCKING (1 item).** The first blocker is fixed: a plate with an off-centre boss is refused again on all 5 probe variants, the same as main. The fix doesn't reach isotropic prisms, though.

### BLOCKING: an isotropic block (cube or near-cube) with an off-centre boss reads a trusted wrong axis

Main refuses every case below as "every axis fits this model equally". The PR head returns `Ok`, `trusted = true`:

| part (2 triangles per box face, boss 72 segments, 1 or 5 bands) | PR head axis | aside |
|---|---|---|
| block 60x60x60 + boss r5 h10 at (10,10) | dir (0.265, 0.265, 0.927) through the block centre | 0.3-0.9 % |
| block 60x60x60 + boss r4 h8 at (15,0) | dir (0.40, 0, 0.91) | 0.2-0.5 % |
| block 60x60x60 + boss r3 h6 at (5,5) | dir (0.148, 0.148, 0.978) | 0.1 % |
| block 60x60x50 + boss r6 h12 at (12,-8) | dir (0.35, -0.23, 0.91) | 0.5-1.8 % |
| block 60x60x80 + boss r5 h10 at (10,10) | dir (0.212, 0.212, 0.954) | 0.2-0.5 % |
| block 60x60x60 + boss r5 h10 at (2,0) | dir (0.057, 0, 0.998) | 0.3 % |

The only turned feature is the boss, about Z at its own centre. Every one of these axes passes through the block centre, is tilted 3-25 degrees, and sets the boss aside as the outlier.

Why the new gates don't catch it:
- The `iso` gate is exactly what lets a cube through. A cube's normal moment is isotropic, so on this branch the eigen candidates are dropped and the face poles are tried.
- The drag of a small boss on a 21600 mm² block is under the 3 %-of-rho tolerance (about 1 mm), so the plain line about the Z pole already passes `judge`. The two-triangle faces' normal lines all meet at the block centre, and the boss supplies the bearings.
- `refine_dir` then tilts the line toward the boss.

So the new area-weighted median and kept-share gates are never exercised here. Even untilted, Z through the block centre is wrong: the boss is 3-15 mm off it.

This is the #208 mechanism, a prism's point-concurrent face lines passing `judge`. But it is a **regression of this PR**: main refuses these parts by name, because the isotropy check ran before any candidate was tried. Either:
- land #208's fix first and stack this PR on it; or
- in the `iso` branch, require that the answering lines meet the pole axis along it, not at one point. For example, require their feet (the stations along the axis where each normal line meets it) to spread over a real share of the part's length, or the concurrent area to be mostly wall around the pole rather than prism faces. Also keep a pole-derived axis from being tilted by `refine_dir` past the noise floor.

Please pin it with a 60 mm cube plus an off-centre r5 boss, refused by name.

### Re-run of the earlier probe set (PR head vs main, same build)
- Plate 100x100x10 + off-centre boss, 5 variants: same as main (4 refused; the (10,0) case is the pre-existing #208).
- Hex bar on end (h 10-200, 1 and 5 bands), L-bracket, D-flats (9 variants), short D-flat with a cross hole: refused on both, unchanged.
- Upright plate + Z boss (10 variants), plate with a centred hole, plate with an off-centre hole: same as main.
- Plate with a hole r45 t30: Z on the PR, refused on main. A gain.
- Short bars r10 h10-h30 (1 and 5 bands), tilted (1,1,1) off-origin r10 h30, discs r50 h10/h20: correct axis, exact. Main refused the short bars and the tilted bar. The intended gain holds.
- Short bar r10 h30 + eccentric pin on its end: Z through the bar, which is correct, with the pin 3-4 % aside (main: refused).
- Ball with two perpendicular flats: Z with 5-7.5 % aside (main: refused). Unchanged since the last round, and not blocking.

### Code checks on the delta
- `lower_half`: the median is weighted by area, it propagates `None` on fewer than `MIN_KEPT` rows or a non-finite area, and indexing is safe. No panics.
- The `iso` gate on LTS is as described. Eigen candidates still win ties, and the result is still deterministic.

Not approved, not merged.
Re-review blocker (cube + off-centre boss, the #208 mechanism) is folded into #208's fix, which is stacked on this branch. #204 merges only back-to-back with #208's PR, never alone.

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
